observed_title: Chernoff’s Inequality - A very elementary proof

read_ranges.scope: Whole paper: theorem/lemma, proof, remarks and complete references

theorem_cards.label: Subset-product bound Eq(1)
assumptions: Indicator Xi, integer k with0<k<βn,0<β<1; no independence required.
theorem_cards.statement: P(ΣXi≥βn)≤[binom(βn,k)]^(−1)Σ_{|S|=k}P(∧_{i∈S}Xi=1). For nonintegerβn interpret falling-product binomial only whereβn>k−1; integer threshold gives tight equality iff sum=βn or sum<k a.s.
proof_steps: For the random count Z=ΣXi, binom(Z,k)=Σ_{|S|=k}∏Xi; its nonnegative expectation is the sum of joint probabilities. On Z≥βn it is at leastbinom(βn,k).
The fixed-success-pattern w_T proof in source is equivalent to Markov for this polynomial.

theorem_cards.label: KL consequence and integer feasibility
assumptions: 0<α<β<1 and k=(β−α)n/(1−α) an admissible integer; everyk-subset all-success probability≤α^k.
theorem_cards.statement: Source consequence P(Z≥βn)≤exp(−nD(β||α)),D=βlog(β/α)+(1−β)log((1−β)/(1−α)). It is not enough that each EXi≤α.
proof_steps: Eq(1) gives binom(n,k)α^k/binom(βn,k); source cites standard entropy estimates for the last bound.
gaps: The article does not print the entropy estimate proof; arbitrary rounding of nonintegerk is not supplied by the text. Keep exact finite combinatorial bound as safe interface unless rounding/optimization is separately derived.

transfer_boundary: Can replace iid by verified fixed-size joint-success control; not by pairwise covariance alone. No conditional Bernstein or time-uniform conclusion. Both pages visually checked.
proof_verification: local derivations and literal errors checked; cited external results not independently certified
